Privacy & site information

Information about inquiry drafts, browser storage and the product details on this site.

Your inquiry

The form creates an email draft in your browser. It does not send your information to LZZ or upload drawings. To contact us, open the draft in your email app, add your attachments and send it yourself.

Saved drafts

Your input stays in this browser tab after a refresh. The form uses sessionStorage to keep a separate draft for each part, service or inquiry topic. It does not save your details to an account or send them to LZZ. Select "Clear saved input" to remove the current draft.

A browser that restores an earlier session may also restore your draft. Clear your input when using a shared device. If storage is blocked or full, you can still prepare a draft while the page is open, then choose "Save draft" to keep a text copy.

Cookies and external services

This site does not use analytics or advertising cookies. Your email provider, WhatsApp and other linked websites have their own privacy policies.

Product and company information

Catalog photographs and labeled illustrations show part examples. They do not replace specifications or inspection records. Workshop photographs and company documents are identified separately.

We use shorter product titles and summaries for easier browsing. The archive retains the original catalog names and source material, even when a page does not display them. These summaries are not independently verified specifications for the pictured parts. Confirm the material grade and tolerances for your own order, together with its inspection and commercial terms.

The engineering guides explain the information needed for an inquiry. They are not inspection reports or customer case studies, and they do not confirm suitability for a particular use. Material filters help you browse existing parts without adding duplicate pages. English summaries of company documents explain their contents; current validity needs separate verification.

Process comparison
Choosing CNC milling, turning or 5-axis machining
On this page

A shaft or sleeve will usually start with turning. A housing with pockets and flat mounting faces is more likely to need milling. Angled features or access to several faces may call for a multi-axis setup. Some parts need a combination; send the drawing so we can review the sequence.

CNC milling operation photographed in LZZ process materials; source folder dated December 2025.
Five-axis machining operation; original LZZ process photograph.
Compare the processes by geometry
CNC turning
Geometry cues

Rotational features such as a shaft, sleeve, disc or fitting, often arranged around an axis.

Drawing and quote questions

Define the datum axis, diameters, shoulders, grooves, threads and runout if required. Confirm whether cross-holes, flats or slots need secondary milling.

CNC milling
Geometry cues

Block-like or irregular forms with pockets, slots, holes, contours and planar mounting faces.

Drawing and quote questions

Define datum faces, pocket depth, hole patterns and positional relationships. Confirm stock, clamping surfaces, setups and inspection records.

Multi-axis machining
Geometry cues

Features distributed over several faces, angled faces or areas that need different tool approaches.

Drawing and quote questions

Define common datums, face-to-face and angular relationships. Review tool access, workholding and sequence against the model.

Parts that need more than one process

A shaft with cross-holes, a turned fitting with milled flats or a housing with angled faces may need more than one operation or setup. The route should preserve the relationships between critical features. Send a 3D model and controlled 2D drawing so the team can review datums, access and inspection together.

Is 5-axis machining always more accurate?

No single process label guarantees accuracy. The achievable result depends on geometry and material, as well as the machine, setup and datum strategy. Finishing and the measurement method also affect acceptance. If an interface matters, state its tolerance and datum on the drawing and ask how it will be produced and checked. Any tolerance target needs feature-specific review.
